ruling.recommended_action: Send to human review: confirm from the driver's GPS/route log (or Ryde ops trip trace) whether the 18:50–19:00 off-route segment [F3] was driven on Defu Avenue 1, the road the rider authorised at 18:47 [F9]; if it was, the segment is exempt under RD-5 and no refund is owed; if it was not on Defu Avenue 1 (or cannot be tied), apply RD-2: 4.09 km × $1.4100/km = $5.77 voucher to the rider. No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so a distance overage flows straight into the fare and RD-2's remedy is the unexempted segment's extra kilometres at this trip's own per-km rate — $34.39 ÷ 24.39 km = $1.4100/km, as the fare facts state [F4][F7][RD-2]. The trace settles the RD-4 element: there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch, so the driver's congestion argument cannot exempt the segment (band 2 on Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway during 18:24–18:50 is corroboration only, and its window closes at 18:50, when the disputed segment begins) [F3][F12][F15][RD-4].

One off-route segment is recorded, 18:50–19:00, 6.93 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.84 km, +4.09 km and up to 884 m from the optimal route [F3][RD-1]. The only candidate exemption left is the rider's consent [RD-5]. I read the chat myself: the driver's 18:46 message asks "ok if I go round via Defu Avenue 1?" [F8] and the rider's 18:47 reply "Can lah, go ahead." [F9] is an agreement, sent before the segment started — so the timing test in RD-5 is met on a complete, fully timestamped chat record [F10][RD-5]. But that agreement names a specific road, so under RD-5 it covers driving on Defu Avenue 1 only, and the record must tie the driven segment to that road.

Nothing in the fact table does. The chat contains no stop, positioning message or road name for the driven path [F8][F9], the route facts give no street name for the segment [F1][F3], and the driver's post-trip statement [F11] is a claim outside the chat that cannot extend consent (G11) and itself names no fact about where the car actually went [RD-5]. Nothing places the segment elsewhere either (no stop the driver chose, no other road named), so this is the scope-unreadable / untied case: the finding on F3 is undetermined under RD-5/G13, not exempt and not automatically counting.

Because that undetermined finding changes the amount — exempt would mean no refund, counting would mean $5.77 — the case goes to a person rather than producing a cash figure, so I rule escalate rather than a partial refund [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. If the human review finds the segment was not on the authorised road, the arithmetic is 4.09 km × $1.4100/km = $5.77 (the remaining $6.40 billed for 4.54 km [F4] is corridor/matching mileage RD-2 does not refund), payable as a voucher under NS-7 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2][NS-7].

There is no rider-named stop in this case, so RD-3 does not apply [F3][F8][F9][RD-3]. No undisclosed add-on is in issue: waiting $0.11, platform $1.47, surge 1.0× are all published items, so FARE-1 gives nothing to refund [F5][F6][F7][FARE-1]. The driver's profile shows 1 upheld dispute in 90 days but 0 upheld route disputes, so even if the deviation were upheld there is no prior upheld route dispute to make this "repeated" under RD-6, and no account flag applies [F18][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the two chat messages, the driver's statement and the rider's complaint in full. "Can lah, go ahead." is agreement; the statement and complaint are about the route and the fare. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the screen is negative [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Evidence status is sufficient: the trace and the fare record settle every measurable element (segment measured, no incident, rate), and the one thing the record cannot settle — whether the driven segment lay on the authorised road — is a reading question I have answered as undetermined, which routes the case to a human by RD-5 itself, not a missing record.
